newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BChem, Danubius hit new high on flat Budapest mkt.
newsitem.headline: BChem, Danubius hit new high on flat Budapest mkt.

text.p: Hungarian share prices remained flat in slow trade on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Tuesday as investors remained on the sidelines waiting for news from Russia and the U.S., traders said.
The BUX index ended at 3,603.75 points, down 3.07. Spot share turnover totalled 853.6 million forints.
"Foreign investors took a wait-and-see stance," said Robert Agoston of Daewoo Securities. "Foreigners did not move too much and when they did so, they were mostly on the selling side."
Agoston added the main reasons for the slow activity were Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery, the U.S. elections and expectations of interim company results.
A few shares, however, ignored all factors of uncertainty and rose to new record highs.

Hotel firm Danubius hit an all-time high of 3,260 forints before finishing at 3,240 forints, up 40. Traders said investors were buying Danubius shares hoping the hotel chain will release strong results for the first nine months.

Chemical firm Borsodchem hit a new peak of 3,315 forints before closing at 3,290, up 35. Agoston said the company's interim results may be influenced by the fact that it halted production due to maintenance works.
Retail chain Global hit a new high at 2,000 forints and traders did not exclude the possibility that its majority owner Tesco Plc was buying the shares.
Global also closed higher at 2,000 forints, up 150.
